name: Polypogon

project_scope.scope: Existing canonical species only; no new admission

look_here_first: INTRODUCED ANNUAL BEARDGRASS: compact soft pale-green cylindrical bottlebrush panicle with a conspicuous HALO of fine bristles derived from many long glume awns. Under 10× magnification identify the awned glumes and very short lemma instead of assuming it is Setaria (whose bristles are reduced sterile branches).

comparison_lesson.title: Annual beardgrass comparison
comparison_lesson.memory_rule: INTRODUCED ANNUAL BEARDGRASS: compact soft pale-green cylindrical bottlebrush panicle with a conspicuous HALO of fine bristles derived from many long glume awns. Under 10× magnification identify the awned glumes and very short lemma instead of assuming it is Setaria (whose bristles are reduced sterile branches).
quick_split: Setaria foxtail bristles attach beneath spikelets as reduced branches, while Polypogon fuzzy awns come from glumes. Phalaris can also form a tight inflorescence but its broad glumes do not give this same long-hair brush. Look at bristle/awn attachment point.
